{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from OAR

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script> -- <SEGMENT>

# OAR resources:
#   -q production
#   -p gpu_model!='NO'
#   -p cluster='grele'
#   -l host=1/gpu=1/core=2,walltime=01:00:00
#   -O ./OUT/oar_job.%jobid%.output
#   -E ./OUT/oar_job.%jobid%.error

# Map to Flux (portable subset): 1 node, 1 task, 2 cores, 1 hour.
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 2
#flux: --time-limit=1h

# Omitted OAR option: -q production (queue)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different priority/limits or wait longer (or be rejected by policy).

# Omitted OAR options: -p gpu_model!='NO' and -p cluster='grele' (resource/property constraints)
# Flux constraint/property selection is site/config dependent; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may land on nodes without GPUs or on a different cluster/architecture, causing failure or slower performance.

# Omitted OAR option: -l gpu=1 (GPU count)
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted OAR options: -O/-E with %jobid% token
# OAR jobid token expansion is not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

source ~/.bashrc
conda activate se

SEGMENT="$1"
if [ -z "$SEGMENT" ]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <SEGMENT>" >&2
  exit 2
fi

CKPT_PATH="../../pretrained_models/A-VAE/A-VAE.pt"
ALGO_TYPE="peem"
DATA_DIR="/srv/storage/talc@storage4.nancy.grid5000.fr/multispeech/corpus/audio_visual/TCD-TIMIT/test_data_NTCD/test_data_5.pkl"
SAVE_ROOT="./results/"

python SE_evaluation.py \
  --segment "$SEGMENT" \
  --ckpt_path "$CKPT_PATH" \
  --algo_type "$ALGO_TYPE" \
  --data_dir "$DATA_DIR" \
  --save_root "$SAVE_ROOT"
"
}
